question: Are @clossys/launcher and @clossys/starter roles under docs/contracts/role-loop-archetypes.json, or executable tooling -- and should the Stage B conformance gates (check-package-conformance.mjs, check-loop-matrix.mjs) keep silently skipping any packages/* manifest absent from the roles map?
options: Exclude both from roles and classify them as executable tooling, as a declared, gate-reported state (not a silent skip): reuse docs/contracts/package-evidence.json's existing category: "executable-tooling" field rather than inventing a second list; report an excluded row for each on the two Stage B gates; make a package in neither the roles map nor executable-tooling (or in both) a hard finding in every mode, not just report mode. Keep both packages in Stage C with a reduced checklist.
Add launcher and starter to role-loop-archetypes.json's roles map as ordinary roles, subject to the full Stage B checklist.
Leave the gates as-is: any packages/* manifest missing from the roles map disappears from both gates with no finding at all.
recommendation: Option 1, confidence high: the owner has already classified both packages this way in their own package.json descriptions, READMEs, and docs/contracts/first-wave-sequence.json's wave kind: "executable-tooling" entries and job text ("without treating executable tooling as a role" / "without treating the scaffolder as a role"); docs/contracts/scope-migration.md's own count is 19 roles across 21 packages, with starter and launcher as executable tooling; neither package has an owned metric under role-loop-archetypes.json's own qualificationVerdicts (every loop either appears to run is already owned by an existing role, yielding extend or compose, never create); and launcher's real output paths (clossys/README.md, etc.) would fail package-framework.json's outputs.pathRule (clossys/<role>/...) by construction if it were graded as a role.
decision: Option 1, as the owner approved it in the coordinator chat on 2026-09-30: Exclude both from roles and classify them as executable tooling, as a declared, gate-reported state (not a silent skip): reuse docs/contracts/package-evidence.json's existing category: "executable-tooling" field rather than inventing a second list; report an excluded row for each on the two Stage B gates; make a package in neither the roles map nor executable-tooling (or in both) a hard finding in every mode, not just report mode. Keep both packages in Stage C with a reduced checklist.
